subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: For failed Codex one-shot or ephemeral runs, should OpenClaw keep using the shared app-server client with lease-aware retirement, move one-shot runs to dedicated clients, or add an explicit transcript-fallback path for cross-provider failover?
rationale: The source shows remaining behavior in multiple ownership areas, and the safe answer depends on maintainer policy for replay safety, shared-client lifecycle cost, and whether fallback providers may receive OpenClaw-native transcript context after a Codex harness failure.

options.title: Dedicated one-shot clients
options.body: Run ephemeral/active-memory Codex one-shots on isolated clients so cleanup cannot retire the main shared client, then separately handle unsupported history shapes as warning/debug policy.

options.title: Keep shared client with stronger leases
options.body: Keep shared-client reuse but add proof that leases cover all active turns and that one-shot retirement cannot close or detach a client needed by a main turn.

options.title: Transcript fallback first
options.body: Focus on feeding OpenClaw-native transcript context to fallback providers, accepting that shared-client cleanup remains a separately tracked lifecycle risk.

recommendation.title: Dedicated one-shot clients
recommendation.body: Run ephemeral/active-memory Codex one-shots on isolated clients so cleanup cannot retire the main shared client, then separately handle unsupported history shapes as warning/debug policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent and merged Codex app-server history makes this the strongest current routing candidate for choosing the repair boundary.
